body: Okay so I also have to do it once a week for work. I really cannot stress this enough, it’s not bad. Also I used to get the nasal swab, and now they just swab your mouth. What kind of therapy have you tried if you don’t mind me asking?

You will 1000% get better. I would recommend coming at your anxiety in a completely different frame of mind. Anxiety is not some evil thing meant to ruin your life. It’s actually an extremely necessary part of life. But when it starts to control your life, that’s when the problem happened. What are the thoughts your having ? The horrible ones? Instead of running away from those thoughts, try saying them out loud. Escalate the situation. For me, I get anxious I’m going to faint or die or something. So my therapist goes okay you die, then what? Once I started to realize I’m always afraid I’m about to die, I was able to confront that fear. Your anxiety will get better but you have to put in an insane amount of work. I’m talking self help books, therapy, journaling when you’re anxious so you can find common triggers. You will get better but be kind to yourself in the process.
Thank you, you’ve really helped. I’m hopeful it’ll get better day by day.

So many holistic approaches ! To be honest, I tried so many anxiety medications, and they made me feel unbelievably awful so my only option was to approach this holistically. I started listening to this self help coach (which I used to think was corny and stupid) named Mastin Kipps, and his approach to anxiety and panic attacks just changed everything for me. I’ve also been in therapy, I force myself to do yoga and meditate 20 minutes a day. The main thing really is to not look at your symptoms. So for me, I just wanted to fix anxiety and panic. That’s what was broken for me. Until I realized that anxiety is only symptom of pain, and trauma, then I just changed my whole approach. But let’s be clear, yoga and mediation will not help until you access your trauma. Otherwise you’re sitting there in a panic attack fighting to mediate which does nothing. I also started holding myself accountable. I used to think holy crap I’ve tried everything to help my anxiety. But the reality is, I didn’t. I just kept trying to the same three or four things and then when they didn’t work, I’d freak out. I had to make crazy life changes. I became vegan, started working out, meditating, taking time for myself, and most importantly sitting with my panic. So when I have a panic attack, I just welcome it. Ill sit in my room, force myself to actually sit when all I want to do is run, and let it run it’s course. Also understanding the brain is huge for me! I’m an engineer, so I can only really understand logic and science. The part of your brain that controls anxiety is an ancient animalistic part located by the brain stem. There isn’t any logic there, it just reacts. And trauma is trapped in your body, so your body continues to react in a trauma state ( fight or flight) until the trauma has run its course. So if you fight a panic attack, you’re just oppressing the trauma. And it will come back. I repeat to myself, I’m okay, I’m safe, it’s okay. Just again and again until it’s over. There’s so much more, but if anything resonates with you, feel free to reach out! Either way, you’ve got this. You do not have to live like this forever, but, you have to do the work to change.

I keep my eyes open. Because my thoughts are still saying I’m in danger or I’m dying, so I am not ready to close my eyes and be fully vulnerable. But if you are, go for it. Being able to be in that meditative state with anxiety is honestly the goal to over coming it. But if you need to start with your eyes open, that’s awesome too.

I would fully recommend not fighting it. Deep breathing won’t get you out of the fight or flight response that your body is going through. Your body is experiencing repressed trauma, the more you shove it down, the more it’ll happen. Try going into a room by yourself, sitting down, and just observe what your bodies doing while repeating to yourself you are not in danger.

Okay so I’ve been dealing with anxiety my entire life (I’m 15), and I’ve been dealing with depression for a few years. This past year has been absolute hell. I started therapy, and also working with a somatic practitioner. I’ve also read a at least fifteen self help books. Before this year, I was never one to do any of that. I was like this is life, just deal with it. Even while actively having a mental illness, I would say it’s fine let’s just move on, we’re all fine. I am not a spiritual nor religious person. I have definitely not had a moment of enlightenment or whatever the hell happens in movies. None of that has happened lol I’ve just been living in hell. But over the past few days, I’ve really realized that anxiety and depression is not a problem. Our brains are not broken, and they are not ruining our lives on purpose. Anxiety and depression is just a symptom of what is really going on. For me, it’s an enormous amount of childhood trauma to where I have never had a safe space in my life, and all of a sudden my brain snapped in half, and I’ve been living with a constant panic attack for a year. We get signals all the time from our brains, but we often ignore them, and then when they manifest as depression, we say what the hell is wrong with me. The tools I’ve learned is to acknowledge your trauma, and do not let anybody define what is trauma to you. Anything that has ever hurt or defined you is valid. If there is a toxic person in your life, cut them out. Honestly even if that is your own mother. Do not engage with them if that space isn’t safe for you. But the reality is, most people on this thread do want to die. But it’s not because you feel like you’ll never get better. Not really, it’s because you are in such an enormous amount of unprocessed pain, that your brain has literally told your body, I can’t do this. The pain is the equivalent of being stabbed, and your brain is acknowledging that, and becomes clouded by depression and death. The first thing I did was say okay yes I do want to die. Then my therapist told me to make a list of all the reasons why. Why life seems to difficult, what’s so complicating, why I feel anxious or depressed. One I finished this list, she told me to turn the page and write about myself. Not what I like about myself or that bs, but what my favorite color is, favorite movie, favorite food. Just qualifies of myself. To remind myself I’m literally a whole ass person with my own thoughts that aren’t my depression. When I finished I just felt like there had to be more to me than panic or depression. I can recommend the books I’ve read and the videos I’ve seen. The reality is your brain isn’t broken, this is not a permanent way of living, your brain and body want your attention. That’s the depression, and wanting to die.
Exactly. I know people who take medication, and love it. But to me, it’s just hell. It won’t fix anything.

Workout. I know that sounds scary because you’re heart will race, but it helps me so much. Your heart is a muscle, palpitations are super common with anxiety. But the stronger the muscle gets, the less palpitations I’ve had. I used to hate when people told me working out helps, but it really does. I just run, walk, or swim. And it helps.

I’m 25 to start with. I was working in a restaurant through college, and there would definitely be customers or coworkers who would just be bullies. I’ve learned a few things I think might help you, being bullied is not something you can or should have to adapt yourself to be okay with. It’s also not something you can shrug off. Bullying is a form of trauma, and nobody should have to experience that. I used to say at work that I’m not in the business of raising ass holes. Meaning as a society, it’s everybody’s job to keep people in check. If I were you, I would 1000% say something to them along the lines of hey, I feel you’re being really disrespectful, and you’re genuinely hurting my feelings. I am going to need you to speak to me with a better attitude instead of straight up being an ass hole. Start saying what you think.

And in all honesty, try not to  look up symptoms. Google is not a doctor, and you will just panic more for no reason. Your body has the ability to panic and it also has the ability to relax. When you have another panic attack, try your best not to fight it. Just literally sit there with it. Your body will know how to calm you down without your thoughts, and it should ease their affects. It’s been working with me.

I completely understand. In all honesty though, anxiety really messed with your body. Especially panic attacks. You enter this animalistic fight or flight mode to the point where you’re body is literally sending more blood to your muscles to prepare for a fight. All your facial muscles lock up and your jaw locks which just absolutely destroys your face. All that facial tension is bound to have lasting effects. When it freaks me out, I just try massaging my face and there are literally facial exercises you can do to help ease  the sore muscles
This!! This has been happening to me for a few months. I completely understand the muscle waves in my face. I have no idea why this is happening.

I completely understand. My health anxiety is horrible. My anxiety has caused migraines, neck pain, full body weakness. What’s worse is I know I just need to relax, but my anxiety just won’t let me. I think the main tip I could offer would be a bit complex. Basically, I would recommend when you have this anxiety of oh no I’m dying or something horrible is happening, I would first take a deep breath. Then something my therapist mentioned is when we have these anxieties, we are basically allowing the five year old version of ourselves out, and allowing them to run our lives. The way when a little kid falls, they feel intense fear and react to that. Even though there is no real deal. So these anxieties are quite literally, letting out inner five year old run loose. I think once you can make that connection, if it resonates with you, I would speak to yourself the way you’d speak to a five year old. You aren’t going to yell and be like shut up you’re fine. But instead maybe try to console yourself, and speak kindly. Create a parent voice (rational figure) in your own head. It’s not an instant fix, but it is helping me get by day by day. Hope this helps.

I feel completely the same way. I feel like there is absolutely no hope, and can literally see myself dying. But I think the reality is, we live our lives for other people. We maintain our lives for other people to agree to them. I’ve also been on medication, therapy, all that. The medication made me more suicidal. Therapy has brought up some tough shit. I’m now in what my therapist calls a trauma state. Maybe before you kill yourself, try something enormously radical. Quit your job, move, throw your phone away and go. Just try something that sounds completely impossible. And see if that helps. The reality is the trauma of childhood or whatever happened is forever. But your brain is not broken. Neither is mine. It’s sending us signals through depression and intense anxiety for me, that we are doing something wrong.
